why: Each query asks how many skills have zero requests inside a time window of fixed length. Sort the queries and the logs by time and slide one window forward, keeping a per-skill request count and the number of skills with a positive count; idle = numSkills - active. This is the binary-search week, but the clean solution is a two-pointer sliding window (binary search only helps the brute force).
hints: Checking every skill for every query is O(numSkills * q), too slow. Notice that all windows have the same length timeWindow.

Answer the queries in increasing time order (remember their original indices). As the window [t - timeWindow, t] moves right, requests only enter at the right and leave at the left: two pointers over the logs sorted by timestamp.
Keep count[skill] and active = number of skills with count > 0; update active when a count goes 0 to 1 or 1 to 0. Sorting dominates: O((L + q) log(L + q)) time, O(numSkills + L + q) space.
pitfalls: The window is inclusive at both ends: [t - timeWindow, t].
A skill with several requests in the window is still one active skill; count skills, not requests.
Restore the original query order in the output after processing sorted queries.
